name: Vesper Null

stars.name: Vesper
stars.notes: Sol-like yellow star wholly veiled by the ink-dark Shroud Nebula, rendering the system invisible to casual survey.

planets.name: Kindling
planets.notes: Cracking lava world whose glow faintly backlights the nebula's inner veil.

planets.name: Censer
planets.notes: Mineral-poor rock passed over by prospectors; hermit legends cling to its single airless moon.

planets.name: Vespertine
planets.notes: Warm shallow seas and reef arcologies; breadbasket and soul of the Veil, home to several million people.

planets.name: Tallow
planets.notes: Wax-pale dune sea used for live-fire exercises by both factions' garrisons, much to each other's annoyance.

planets.name: Nightwatch
planets.notes: Helium-3 skimming giant whose storm bands swallow unlicensed tankers whole; the refueling point of record.

planets.name: Pale Sister
planets.notes: Glacier-shelled world with a subsurface ocean pinged once by probes; results sealed under Concord writ.

planets.name: Far Candle
planets.notes: Dim outlier carrying an automated navigation beacon maintained by whoever remembers to.

planets.name: The Mooring
planets.notes: Captured rogue world hanging at the system's edge; smugglers use its shadow as a staging anchor.

anomalies.name: The Null Veil
anomalies.location: system-wide within the Shroud Nebula shell
anomalies.notes: Space folds light around the nebula so sensors return ghosts and jump bearings skew by degrees; the system's best defense.

anomalies.name: Vesper Echo
anomalies.notes: Lightning-like discharges crawl the nebula shadow here, imposing rolling comms blackouts that both fleets blame for friendly-fire incidents.

asteroid_belts.name: Debris of the Splitting
asteroid_belts.notes: Wreck-field from the Concord-Assembly fleet action; salvagers work it under flag-of-truce rules.

asteroid_belts.name: Shroudline Belt
asteroid_belts.notes: Cometary debris harvested for volatiles by Nightwatch skimming crews between runs.

stations.name: High Vesper Orbital
stations.notes: The Veil's great market ring, jointly administered and endlessly argued over.

stations.name: Beacon Null
stations.location: inner edge of the Shroud Nebula
stations.notes: Freehold Assembly fortress guarding the only reliable jump corridor through the fold.

stations.name: Skimward Platform
stations.notes: Helium-3 refining ring feeding tanker convoys bound for three sectors.

faction_control.notes: The Concord administers High Vesper and Vespertine while the Freehold Assembly holds Beacon Null; armistice patrols shadow every convoy through the fold.

history: Hidden for centuries inside the Shroud, the system was revealed when a Concord jump liner tore a navigable breach through the nebula's fold.
Vespertine was colonized within a generation, its reef cities growing into the commercial heart of the Veil almost overnight.
The Assembly's seizure of Beacon Null triggered the Splitting, a brief fleet battle ended by armistice that froze the standoff now defining the system.
description: Vesper Null is a yellow sun wearing a burial shroud. The ink-dark Shroud Nebula swallows its light entirely, folding space so thoroughly that the system went undiscovered until a jump liner punched through by accident. Inside hides a full spread of eight worlds around a sol-like star, from lava-lit Kindling to the captured sentinel called The Mooring.

It should be a quiet garden world system, and Vespertine tries to be one, all warm shallows and reef arcologies beneath High Vesper's roaring market ring. But geography is destiny here: the Null Veil makes the nebula nearly impassable except along one corridor, and whoever holds the corridor holds the trade of three sectors. The Concord and the Freehold Assembly have been frozen in armed truce over that question since the Splitting.

Visitors come for the markets and stay wary of everything else. Comms die without warning in the Echo zone, sensor ghosts walk the shroudline, and the Concord has sealed all survey data from Pale Sister's subsurface ocean without explanation. Old spacers say the nebula hides more than one star, and that some lights seen between the folds are not reflections at all.
